title.value: The generalizability of pre-processing techniques on the accuracy and fairness of data-driven building models: A case study
title.justification: The title explicitly states the focus on analyzing pre-processing techniques for data-driven building models, with an emphasis on accuracy and fairness.
title.quote: The generalizability of pre-processing techniques on the accuracy and fairness of data-driven building models: A case study

extractions.description: This paper examines the effectiveness of different pre-processing techniques on the accuracy and fairness of data-driven building models (DDBMs) used for predicting lighting status in buildings. It introduces a new technique called sequentially balanced sampling (SBS) and compares it with existing methods to handle data distribution imbalances. The study conducts simulations on lighting data to evaluate these techniques in terms of their impact on predictive accuracy and fairness, with implications for improving DDBM performance.

primary_category.justification: The focus on improving the predictive performance of building management systems through data-driven models aligns with efforts to optimize energy consumption and reduce emissions in the building sector, which is crucial for climate change mitigation.
primary_category.quote: In recent years, buildings and building construction sectors have become data rich, due to the rapidly popularity of Internet of Things (IoT) and building management systems (BMS)... These data could be used as a basis to develop data-driven building models (DDBMs) to predict indoor air temperature, energy consumption, thermal comfort, occupancy status/numbers, indoor air quality, fire hazard or HVAC system performance.
